text:
Sasha: Quick idea for the streaming/retry case we saw in prod this morning — propose introducing an "ingress stream fence" to delimit the replayable prefix vs commit-side effects. short version: gateway stamps a fence-id on stream open, proxies can replay/hedge only up to the fence; once backend emits a fence-ack, we treat subsequent tokens as non-replayable and switch to fast-path.

Kevin: hmm — can you sketch the state machine? worried about memory and long-lived streams.

Sasha: sure. minimal model: OPEN -> REPLAYABLE (fence set) -> FENCE_ACK -> COMMITTED. If a retry/hedge happens in REPLAYABLE we can replay prefix safely. After FENCE_ACK we stop any speculative replays; if upstream fails we fallback to compatible model variant.

Maria: client compatibility question — will this require client-side changes? mobile/web SDKs?

Sasha: opt-in on client for strongest guarantees. default behavior is unchanged (best-effort resume). clients that want exactly-once semantics for side-effects can flip fence=true on stream start.

AJ: two quick infra questions: 1) how do we bound prefix buffering? 2) what does KV cache look like across hedged connections?

Sasha: good call. plan is configurable prefix window (time + bytes). default: 250ms OR 8KB. KV cache keyed by (fence-id, request-id) so we can reuse prefix results during replay, then drop when fence-ack arrives or TTL expires. minimizes long-term memory.

Kevin: can you show a sample gateway config?

Sasha: yep — example config for per-route opt-in:

```yaml
routes:
  - path: /v1/stream
    streaming: true
    streamFence:
      enabled: true
      windowMs: 250
      maxPrefixBytes: 8192
      fallbackPolicy: fallback-to-variant
```

Kevin: nice. fallbackPolicy sounds important. what are supported values?

Sasha: initial set: `fallback-to-variant` (switch to CPU-tiny model), `queued-retry` (wait for dedicated capacity), `fail-fast` (return error). could expand later.

infra-bot: [metric] stream_fence.buffered_prefix_bytes gauge now available on staging. collect with label=route.

Maria: perf/regression concern — how much latency does the fence add to first-byte? we need numbers for product.

AJ: I'll run a 1k-stream-per-second canary with fence enabled and compare p50/p95. expecting small overhead for the stamp (couple ms) and potential memory churn on heavy concurrency.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: architecture/stage -> canary group at 10% in 20m. CI: https://ci.internal/runs/6789

Kevin: edge-case: what if client disconnects after fence-ack and we have side-effect partially applied upstream? do we need a compensation API?

Sasha: yes — we need developer guidance. docs should recommend idempotency tokens for side-effects and provide a flow for compensation reconciles. also suggestion: expose fence lifecycle via Console (trace per request).

Maria: sounds reasonable. product will draft docs and add an example using webhooks + fence semantics.

AJ: quick implementation note: runtime needs a small per-connection struct (fence-id, prefix-buffer len, replayable flag). should be a cheap allocation pooled per worker. I'll prototype in runtime repo and push a draft RFC PR.

Sasha: TL;DR tradeoffs: + reduces double-side-effects during hedging/reconnects, + explicit opt-in avoids breaking existing clients, - extra per-connection state, - increased complexity in rollouts.

Sasha: action items: (1) AJ prototype PR for runtime + unit tests, (2) infra: wire metrics + dashboard (infra-bot), (3) docs: product writeup + example (Maria), (4) schedule canary and perf run (Kevin/AJ).

Kevin: ACK, will coordinate canary window.

Maria: will assign docs task in the next sprint.

AJ: starting prototype today, will post PR link when ready.

Sasha: thanks — marking this thread resolved for now, will follow up with RFC link and perf numbers. :thumbsup:
